66653970596e: What does the narrator suggest about Scrooge by saying he “was not a man to be frightened by echoes”?
He is stubborn and refuses to admit fear
He is deaf and cannot hear the noise
He enjoys loud noises in his house
He has already met the ghosts before
Though the sound “resounded through the house like thunder,” Scrooge calmly “fastened the door” and climbed the stairs, showing his stubborn refusal to be alarmed.
Why does the narrator describe getting a hearse up the staircase “broadwise”?
To exaggerate how wide and gloomy the staircase is
To explain how Scrooge moved his furniture
To show that Scrooge owns a hearse
To describe a real accident on the stairs
The hyperbole stresses size: “There was plenty of width for that, and room to spare,” which helps explain why Scrooge “thought he saw a locomotive hearse going on before him in the gloom.”
What mood does the passage mainly create?
Details like “it was pretty dark with Scrooge's dip” and the imagined hearse are eerie, while the joke about a “bad young Act of Parliament” adds humour.
1624a148d194: What does Sara’s reaction show about her character?
She has a deep love of books and learning
She wants to be paid for helping
She is afraid of reading alone

Sara promised to give her a present
She will not have to go to school

She is out of breath from running
She is about to cry from sadness

e63227386349: What is the effect of comparing the theatre to “a festive ark”?
It makes the theatre seem a bright, floating refuge amid dull surroundings
It suggests the theatre is about to sink
It shows the theatre is a religious building
It proves the theatre is near the sea

How does the music affect the young man?
It stirs up the restless feeling he has had all day
It calms him so he forgets his worries
It makes him want to join the band
It annoys him and he walks away
The waltz’s “languor and supple movement, evoked the incommunicable emotion which had been the cause of all his day’s unrest.”
How does the final sentence change the tone of the passage?
It breaks the dreamy mood with an ordinary, slightly comic interruption
It deepens the romantic mood of the waltz
It introduces a sudden real danger

e4e396976cfd: What does Darnay’s reaction to Mr. Lorry’s parting words suggest?
He secretly knows he may not be there to care for them
He does not love Lucie anymore
He thinks Mr. Lorry is joking
He is glad to be rid of his family
When asked to “take precious care of them,” Darnay “shook his head and doubtfully smiled,” hinting at his plan to leave for Paris.

To explain his trip and reassure his family that he will be safe
To ask the Doctor for money for the journey
To apologize for an argument with Lucie
To invite Lucie to join him in Paris

The letters were “fervent” because he wrote them with deep emotion, “dwelling on the same topics with the strongest assurances.”
8286e9b7ae1f: What makes the Duchess funny in this passage?

She thinks it will be easy

She just agrees with Alice calling mustard a mineral
She owns a real mustard farm
She wants to take Alice there

4abac261f76e: How do the other animals react to the dogs’ attack?
They are shocked and frightened into silence
They try to fight off the dogs
They ignore it and keep working

They are trained and controlled by someone powerful
They are wild strays from the forest

05b4440a29f8: What does Dora’s description of Mirabel suggest about Mirabel?

01b2fe3839f7: What does the description of the trees mainly show about October?

a8321f2db09b: What is the effect of describing the governess as presiding “with the cold impartiality of a Goddess of Battles”?

8a0a57be7223: Why does Harry wonder what Mrs. Fowler has written?

03725baffacb: What is the effect of the simile describing the wine as flowing “like new blood”?

7265ca1d4f3b: What is happening to the narrator as the dust dances?
